text.aura: Your aura is tall-tree energy. Before you speak, people sense direction: this person knows where they're going and probably has a plan for getting there. Gap carries a clean, upright presence that reads as dependable and a little bit in charge. It's the aura of the friend everyone calls when the group trip falls apart. There's warmth in it, but it's structured warmth, like shade from a big tree on a hot day. Your glow isn't sparkle. It's steadiness that slowly makes people feel safer. When you're at your best, you look like someone who has grown into exactly the right shape. The glow-up for you isn't becoming someone softer or flashier. It's letting that natural backbone show without apologizing for how much space it takes.
text.how-people-read-you: First impression: capable, serious, slightly intimidating. Strangers assume you're older or more senior than you are, and they often ask you for directions, advice or the wifi password. That's the tree effect. Second impression, once they know you: loyal, funny in a dry way, surprisingly sentimental about old photos. The gap between the two is where people get you wrong. Some think you're judging them when you're just concentrating. Your resting expression says "I'm handling it," which is great at work and less great at a party where you'd like someone to come talk to you. A small change helps: an open posture, a smile that arrives a second earlier, a question instead of a solution. People don't need you to be less strong. They need a door into the warmth.
text.colors: Your home palette is Wood: forest green, moss, sage, deep teal. These read as calm authority on you, like you were born wearing them. Water colors support you beautifully too, because Water feeds Wood in the five elements: navy, ink blue, charcoal. A navy coat over a green knit is basically your signature. For a lift, add a little Fire: a terracotta scarf, a rust bag, a coral lip. It warms up your serious energy and makes you look more approachable in photos. Silver and stark white work best as one clean accent rather than head to toe, where they can make your aura read rigid rather than strong. Natural textures matter as much as color for you: linen, wool, wood beads, anything that looks like it grew somewhere.
text.style: Your style is grounded classic with a long silhouette. Think structured blazers, straight-leg trousers, long coats, clean shirts, boots you could actually walk in. You look best in pieces with clear lines that echo your upright energy, nothing fussy, nothing that looks like it's trying too hard. Quality over quantity suits you; one good bag beats five trendy ones. Where you can play: one unexpected detail per outfit. A vintage brooch, a patterned sock, a bold earring. It hints at the funny, sentimental person underneath the competence. Hair and makeup lean natural and polished rather than dramatic. Your best "glow-up photo" is outdoors, in daylight, near trees or old architecture, standing tall, looking slightly off-camera like you just remembered something good.
text.vibe: The vibe to aim for is the gentle leader. Same backbone, softer edges. The shift isn't in your clothes so much as your energy: asking instead of announcing, laughing at yourself more, letting other people take the lead on small things. Picture a K-drama CEO character in episode twelve, after they've learned to be kind. That's your arc. Try a few experiments. Compliment someone without adding advice. Wear something soft, like a cashmere knit or a flowy shirt, on a day you feel strong. Post a photo where you're laughing instead of composed. Make one decision just because it's fun, not because it's correct. Your aura gets warmer every time you show that strength and playfulness can live in the same person.
text.aura-dims: Your aura dims when you're overextended, carrying everyone's plans and nobody's carrying yours. It shows as stiffness: shorter replies, a tense jaw, outfits that drift into the same gray uniform because deciding anything else feels like too much. You start looking efficient instead of alive. The reset for you is growth in small form. Go somewhere green and walk without a destination. Learn something useless and fun. Put on the green thing you love and leave the laptop closed for an evening. Rearrange one corner of your room so it feels new. And say no to one request this week, without a long explanation. Trees grow best with space around them. When you give yourself some, the glow comes back on its own.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gap, your aura is pure tall-tree energy. People feel safe the second you walk in.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also feel like you're about to assign them a task.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Forest green and navy on you? Main character in a quiet K-drama.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Your resting face says "I'm handling it." Relax the jaw, CEO.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your glow-up is soft strength. Same backbone, warmer smile.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: One fun accessory. One. Prove you have a silly side.

spring.intro: A spring birthday puts your own element in charge, so a spring Gap Wood aura arrives fully grown. People read you as capable and upright before you open your mouth, the friend who obviously knows where the restaurant is. In-season Wood can look a little too much like hard work, though: practical layers, sensible bags, a palette of every green you own. Your glow-up is about edges. Metal, the element that prunes Wood, is your best stylist: one crisp white shirt, a structured blazer, silver hardware, a clean tailored line. Keep a single forest or olive piece as your signature and let the rest be sharp. You look most like yourself when you look deliberately trimmed.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Gap, four shades of green is a forest, not an outfit. Add one silver edge.

summer.intro: Born under summer's Fire, a Gap Wood spends its own element feeding the heat, so your aura reads as generous and energetic: the person organizing the beach day and carrying the cooler. Because your Wood is busy fueling the season, your look can drift toward whatever is easy and quick, and by August you are dressed like a volunteer. Your glow-up is restoring depth. Water is your resource, so navy, ink and deep teal calm the heat and make you look composed rather than rushed. Pair them with natural linen and a wooden or woven accessory to keep your roots visible. The summer Gap glow is a tall tree casting cool shade: relaxed, grounded, quietly in charge.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Gap, deep teal linen and a woven bag. You'll look like shade on a hot day.

autumn.intro: Arriving when Metal rules, the element that cuts Wood, an autumn Gap Wood carries an aura shaped by pressure. People read you as disciplined, serious and possibly a little strict. Your style tends toward tailoring already, sometimes so much that it looks like armor, all stiff collars and sensible grays. Your glow-up is letting the tree show through the uniform. Water softens Metal and feeds Wood, so deep blues work beautifully, and a touch of moss or sage reminds people you are alive under the structure. Try one texture that moves, like a chunky knit or a soft scarf, against your sharp coat. You are at your most magnetic when the discipline looks chosen, not imposed.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Gap, that coat could survive an audit. Throw a moss scarf over it and smile.

winter.intro: Winter's Water feeds Wood, which gives a winter Gap Wood deep roots and a bare canopy. Your aura comes across as calm, thoughtful and slightly unreachable, the tall quiet one at the back of the photo. Navy and charcoal dominate your wardrobe because they feel safe, and they are, but they let you disappear into the season. Your glow-up is warmth. Fire is what a winter tree needs, so bring in rust, terracotta, a camel coat or a red scarf that catches light. Keep one green signature piece, a bag or a beanie, where people see it first so your Wood stays visible. Suddenly people describe you as approachable. Nothing changed except the temperature of your colors.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Gap, one rust scarf and you go from 'serious' to 'come sit with us'.

earth.intro: In the Earth days, the last weeks of a season, a Gap Wood aura is a tall tree in heavy soil: grounded, capable and a bit serious. People read you as the reliable one who has things handled. Your wardrobe may lean practical and earthy, all khaki and tan. Your glow-up is lift. Water feeds Wood, so deep navy and ink blue refresh you, and a clear green brings your own element forward. Swap one beige layer for something with a clean line and some height. The late-season Gap glow is a tree after rain: taller than you remembered.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Gap, trade one tan layer for ink blue. Instant height.

strength.strong: A strong Gap Wood aura fills a doorway. With plenty of Wood and Water in your chart, you come across as commanding, upright and certain, and your style tends to repeat that message loudly: big coats, bold boots, the same strong silhouette every single day. The blind spot is pushing. Your look can read as a decision already made, which quietly stops people from approaching. Soften one element at a time. Swap a stiff layer for something fluid, add a warm color, let one accessory be playful or even a little silly. People still see the tree. Now they also see the leaves.
strength.weak: A weak Gap Wood aura wants to stand tall but often slouches into the background. With little Wood or Water support, you may dress to blend in, borrowing friends' taste or reaching for whatever feels safe and invisible. The blind spot is shrinking: wearing clothes that apologize for taking up space. Your glow-up starts with one tall, confident piece, a long coat, a strong boot, a structured bag in forest green or navy. Build the rest of the outfit around it. Wear it on an ordinary Tuesday, not just to events. Gap Wood is meant to be seen from a distance, and you deserve to be.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood gives your aura lots of drive and upward energy, but it can read as restless or intense, always busy, always growing. Your style may lean practical and outdoorsy, sometimes at the expense of polish. Balance it with Metal touches: a crisp white shirt, silver jewelry, cleaner lines, one tailored piece. Declutter your wardrobe so what remains feels intentional. Your glow is strongest when your ambition looks calm, like a tall tree that doesn't need to prove it's growing.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means your aura can lack a sense of freshness and new beginnings. You might stick to the same outfits for years or feel unsure about trying new styles. Bring in Wood: greens, botanical prints, natural fabrics like linen and cotton, plants in your space. Try one new style element each month, a different silhouette, a new accessory, a new hair clip. Growth looks good on you. Let your style evolve a little, the way spring changes a garden.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your aura bright, bold and sometimes overwhelming. Whether you wear it loudly or quietly, your look can carry more heat than the moment needs: one statement too many, or an intensity people feel before you've said a word. Balance it with Water: navy, deep blue, black accents, calmer silhouettes. Choose one statement per outfit instead of five. Let some quiet into your presence too, listening more, moving slower. Your glow is already strong. Cooling it slightly makes it look richer and more confident.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means your aura can feel understated, sometimes so understated that people overlook you. You might default to neutrals and avoid anything that draws attention. Bring in Fire: a red lip, a coral scarf, warm gold jewelry, a little shimmer. Seek out sunlight in photos and in life. Let yourself be seen in small ways: post the photo, wear the bright thing, laugh openly. Visibility is a skill, and it looks lovely on you when you allow it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth gives you a grounded, warm aura that can slide into heavy or overly practical. Your wardrobe may be comfortable but samey, lots of beige, brown and safe basics. Balance it with Wood: fresh greens, lighter fabrics, a playful print, something that moves when you walk. Try one unexpected piece. Rearrange your space for a fresh feeling. Your stability is beautiful. A little lightness on top keeps it from looking stuck.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth can make your aura feel scattered or ungrounded, lots of ideas, many style moods, not much consistency. Your outfits may change wildly depending on your mood. Bring in Earth: camel, beige, warm brown, ochre, and solid basics like a good coat and reliable shoes. Build a small capsule wardrobe you can trust. Ceramics, wood and warm lighting at home help too. When your foundation is steady, your creativity looks intentional instead of chaotic.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives your aura sharpness and polish that can tip into cold or severe. Your style may be immaculate but a little untouchable: very clean lines, lots of black, white and gray, everything controlled. Balance it with Fire: warm colors near your face, soft textures, a smile that comes sooner. Let one thing be imperfect on purpose, rolled sleeves, tousled hair, a playful accessory. Precision is your strength. Warmth makes it inviting.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal can make your aura feel soft but a little undefined. People like you, but they might not remember your style clearly. Bring in Metal: silver jewelry, crisp white, sharp tailoring, clean shoes, a structured bag. Edit your wardrobe so every piece earns its place. A clear signature, the same ring, the same scent, a consistent color, gives your look definition. Clarity doesn't make you colder. It makes you memorable.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water gives your aura depth and mystery, but it can read as distant, moody or hard to reach. You might hide in dark colors and oversized layers. Balance it with Earth: warm neutrals near your face, structured pieces, a grounded silhouette. Add a little Fire too, a coral or rose accent, to bring warmth. Let people see your expression clearly. Your mystery is magnetic. A bit of warmth makes it feel welcoming, not unreachable.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means your aura can feel busy and bright without much depth or calm. You might always be on, always moving, with little stillness. Bring in Water: navy, midnight blue, black, flowing fabrics, a more relaxed silhouette. Create quiet moments in your day and let them show in your style, softer textures, fewer accessories. Water by your bed and slow evenings help your energy settle. Depth looks good on you. Give it some room.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your warmth is your magic. Let navy or stone frame it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: beige, oatmeal, sand, more beige. You look like a very calm cupboard.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is beautiful. One silver piece or a deep blue lifts it.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: you look expensive and impossible to talk to. Add one soft texture.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your polish is stunning. A warm knit lets people come closer.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: all black, all mystery, all the time. Even vampires wear burgundy.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is magnetic. A warm color helps people find the door.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Try a sage scarf or a leafy print. Let your style grow a little.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Same outfit since 2021 isn't a signature. It's a rut with good lighting.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? A coral scarf or warm gold earrings changes how people greet you.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: Head-to-toe gray says 'don't notice me'. Is that really the message?

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? A camel coat or a terracotta bag grounds your whole look.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Five trends this month, zero signature. Commit to something longer than a week.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? A crisp white shirt or a silver cuff gives your look clean edges.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Everything slightly creased and slightly oversized reads accidental. Tailor one piece.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? Deep navy or a fluid silk adds calm depth to your look.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Always bright, always on. Let one outfit be quiet. People lean in.
